# Hardening notes — hogee run-12

Hunter hardening notes kept in ledger bookkeeping (not findings; no verdicts). Grouped by hunter.

**h-anchor**

- anchor.sh step 5/6: pass explicit --nonce, --gas-limit (about 21000 + 16 per calldata byte plus a margin) and fee caps to cast mktx. Enforce the same ceilings and type == eip1559 both in the jq predicate and in checkRawTx (which today does not check the tx type that checkSepoliaAnchor later requires). Print the maximum cost (gas x maxFeePerGas) in the [y/N] text.
- anchor.sh: drain pending stdin (for example a read -t 0 loop) before the [y/N] read at line 163, so type-ahead entered during signing cannot answer the one publish prompt.
- anchor.sh: cast runs in $W/cwd, which has no foundry.toml. Foundry's project-root search walks ancestors for foundry.toml and loads that root's .env, which does not override variables already set but can set ETH_GAS_PRICE, ETH_PRIORITY_GAS_PRICE, ETH_GAS_LIMIT or CHAIN. With TMPDIR unset, W lands under /private/tmp, where another local user could plant both files. Writing an empty foundry.toml into $W/cwd stops the search there. Chain, recipient, value and input stay guarded either way (Foundry behaviour to confirm).
- anchor.sh: cast and alloy error text may include ETH_RPC_URL (reqwest 'error sending request for url (...)') and a node's JSON-RPC message verbatim on stderr. That contradicts 'it is never printed' (same-user terminal only). Consider filtering cast stderr through a control-character and URL scrub.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/crypto.ts parseSignedTx: require EIP-2 low-s (as recoverEcdsa already does) and a canonical round trip (serializeTransaction(parsed incl. signature) == raw). Then each signed anchor has exactly one txHash that can pass offline, and a malleated, non-includable variant cannot show a dead Etherscan link with a pass.
- docs/fisco/ANCHOR.md says 'a forger with the key could invent a block number or time'. In fact anyone holding the public raw tx can rewrite a real anchor's receipt and block number and time and still pass offline. Reword this, and label the time as unconfirmed offline wherever it is shown.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/anchor-cli.ts: the sidecar is read once for the online line and again for the offline line (cli.ts:157). Read it once and pass the same bytes to both, so the two lines always judge the same file.
- scripts/redteam/src/fisco/rpc.ts httpTransport: res.json() has no response-size cap. A hostile Sepolia RPC can make fisco:sepolia-code or fisco:anchor capture buffer an unbounded body until the 30 s timeout. Cap the body (for example 4 MiB) before parsing.
- scripts/redteam/src/fisco/anchor.ts captureAnchor polls the same RPC that received cast publish. Optionally confirm the receipt and block with confirmSepoliaAnchor against a second, independent RPC before writing the sidecar.

**h-api**

- packages/api/src/evidence/fisco-store.ts:179-180 (with store.ts:47): readFiscoFile buffers each pack file whole (up to 4 MiB) and copies it into a new Uint8Array. Before that, every request re-reads pack.json (up to 4 MiB), re-reads and zod-parses the source bundle's three index files (up to 12 MiB) and re-walks the pack, with no concurrency bound. This is the documented open L10 at a smaller cap, and the Proof page triggers it once per listed file (up to 400, 8 in parallel). Fix: stream from the opened handle, bounded to the checked size (as the mock's bodyOf does), and reuse one tenancy and walk answer per pack.
- packages/api/src/evidence/fisco-store.ts:178-179: any file in a pack folder whose name passes BundlePath is listed and served, not only the verifier's isPackPath allow-list (tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/pack.ts:103-104). A stray file left in a pack folder (an editor backup, a note) is served to every reader of the source bundle. Fix: keep listing every entry, so the browser check fails as the CLI does, but serve only isPackPath paths.
- packages/api/src/evidence/fisco-store.ts:130-137: MAX_LISTED_PACKS = 20 is applied by folder mtime before the tenant filter. 20 newer packs of another deployment sharing the evidence root therefore hide this tenant's packs (the documented open item 3 for runs, at a 10x smaller cap). Fix: filter by tenancy before the slice, or align the cap with MAX_LISTED_RUNS.
- packages/api/src/evidence/fisco-store.ts:101-114: packEntries applies the 400-entry cap only after readdir has returned a whole directory, and folders entered at depths 0-1 never count toward it. A pack folder holding very many entries or empty sub-folders costs a full directory read on every request. Fix: use opendir and count folders. The disk content is operator-controlled.
- packages/api/src/evidence/store.ts:46-47: readInside checks the size with fh.stat() and then calls fh.readFile(), which takes its own fstat. A file appended between the two is read past maxBytes, whereas the mock's readUpTo caps at the checked size. This needs a concurrent local writer. Fix: read exactly the checked size from the descriptor.

**h-chain**

- prepare_chain_dir (lib.sh:136-154) adopts any existing, user-owned, non-git directory without requiring that it be empty or already marked. refuse_unsafe_dir refuses home and its ancestors, but not an ancestor of the repo or worktree, ~/Desktop, ~/Documents, iCloud Drive or ~/Library/CloudStorage: for example --dir ~/Library or --dir ~/hogee-wt passes. chain-down --wipe then deletes it with rm -rf. Only the operator chooses --dir, so this is not a finding. Adopt a directory only if it is empty or already carries its own marker, and refuse a D that contains any protected path.
- selftest_procargs (chain-check.sh:145-165) checks only the environment through ps -E, which P1's macOS never shows, so the kern.procargs and kern.proc deny is never actually exercised. Probe a canary in a sleeping process's argv, which ps shows unsandboxed on every macOS.
- The listen probes bind only 127.0.0.1. Add a probe that a chain port cannot be bound on 0.0.0.0 or a LAN address under node.sb, so the loopback part of the bind rule is tested, not just assumed from SBPL's 'localhost' semantics.
- Post-build checks look for symlinks only (find -type l), safe_target does not check the link count, and hard-link creation is probed only under node.sb, not build.sb. Add a link-count check (stat -f %l = 1) to safe_target and owned_file, and a build.sb hard-link probe to the self-test and profiles.sh.
- chain-check does not tie the listeners to node pids. It checks that whatever answers 127.0.0.1:8545 and :8546 serves chain 0x4ee8 and node0's head and hash, and that node sockets are on 127.0.0.1, but not that the LISTEN sockets on 8545 and 20200 belong to node0 and 8546 to node4. Add per-port lsof pid checks. node.sb's port list is also profile-wide (any node may bind 8545 or 8546); a per-node port parameter would make that separation sandbox-enforced.
- The observer-proposal cast send (chain-up.sh:248-250) and forge script (deploy.sh:162-165) take the chain id from the node. Pass --chain 20200 explicitly, even though only throwaway keys sign.
- The dead-proxy egress block is checked at foundry_egress_check time only. A later listener on 127.0.0.1:9 (ports below 1024 are bindable without root on current macOS) would turn it into a live proxy for the rest of a long forge run. Re-check before each Foundry invocation, or use a port that is not commonly bindable.
- Both profiles could explicitly deny the inherited data writes to .CFUserTextEncoding (including ~/.CFUserTextEncoding) and file creation in /cores. The README documents both but does not need them.

**h-check**

- scripts/redteam/src/fisco/sepolia-code.ts:126 writes error.message to stderr without nodeText. captureSepoliaCode (line 62) calls Number(BigInt(head.number)) on a string served by the Sepolia capture RPC, and V8's SyntaxError message embeds that string, so a hostile https RPC can put ESC/OSC sequences on the operator's terminal. Wrap the line in nodeText as fisco/cli.ts:213 and anchor.ts:227 do, and check head.number with a quantity regex before BigInt.
- Makefile:66-70: the recipe passes PACK safely, but the arguments are then re-quoted by pnpm's script-argument handling (pnpm 12.11.2, outside the repo). Running node --import tsx src/fisco/cli.ts directly from tools/verify-evidence, as replay.sh does for the replay, removes that second shell parse.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/deploy.ts: without --artifacts (no contracts/out), artifacts.json deployedBytecode, code/*.hex and code-sepolia/*.hex are only compared with each other, never with the pinned creation bytecode. Require each deployedBytecode (immutables zero) to appear inside its artifact.bytecode (TreasuryGovernance's inside Treasury's) so the runtime code is bound to the pinned broadcast.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/ledger.ts:56 compares hashObject(ledger.blocks) with node0Keccak, but scripts/redteam/src/fisco/ledger.ts:166-180 computes node0Keccak over the very array it writes as ledger.blocks. The comparison always passes and proves nothing offline. Reword the ok line, or keep independent node0 data for the blocks that hold no pack tx.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/ledger.ts:81-88 accepts any regulator nonce-0 CommitteeManager tx with the proposal log as the observer proposal. Its input keccak is unchecked, proposalBlock is not required to be <= headAtStart, and G0's nonce is not required to be 1.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/view.ts:259-286: blockOrder compares block numbers only. Steps in the same block are not required to follow seq order by transactionIndex, yet seq-based derivations such as pausedBefore for R17 assume it. Blocks are also keyed by the served quantity string, so mixed-case numbers skip the two-hash and parent checks (the ledger check's BigInt comparison compensates). The served block transactions lists in txs/*.json are never compared with node4's lists.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/view.ts:121-127: an absent or zero-filled logsBloom on a receipt with logs only adds to the 'not served' note and never fails.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/regulator.ts: the checker never requires roles.regulator to differ from the FINAL roles or the deployer; only the replay's senderRoles enforces it. regulator == agent is caught only indirectly, by the ledger's G0 rule.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/load.ts:61 and tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/t28.ts:44 use the in operator, so index or pin entries named after Object.prototype members are never reported as missing. This is harmless, but Object.hasOwn would be exact.
- tools/verify-evidence/src/fisco/cli.ts:39 printable leaves other Unicode format characters unescaped (U+061C, U+200B-U+200D, U+2060-U+2064, U+FEFF, U+00AD), which nodeText's Cf class covers. None of them is a terminal control or a line break.

**h-gov**

- cli.ts:126 calls privateKeyToAccount(regulatorKey) without the wrapper the worker uses for FINAL keys (apps/worker/src/config/keys.ts:54-60). For an out-of-range scalar, noble's error message includes the value, and cli.ts:213 prints error.message to stderr. This is unreachable in practice: replay.sh's keystore_address has cast derive the address from the same keystore first, and the key is throwaway. Wrapping it the same way would close the gap.
- owned_file (lib.sh:189-191) checks D/keys/regulator.json and D/keys/pw (replay.sh:103,149), and D/facts/sdk files go through regulator_fact_problems. Neither checks the link count, and chain-check.sh's unexpected_links finds only symlinks, so a hard link to a file outside D would pass. Only the operator can write D/keys and D/facts (mode 700, outside every sandbox's write set), and senderRoles still pins the decrypted key to the genesis admin, so this is not a finding. Adding a stat -f %l == 1 check would make it explicit.
- Every published pack carries the raw signed txs of the real FINAL keys: legacy type, chainId 20200, gasPrice 0, value 0, including the new F1/M1 agent txs. 20200 is the chain id the mirror keeps from FISCO's default config, so those bytes can be rebroadcast on any other network with chain id 20200 and no fee floor. The FINAL addresses would then appear as senders there. There is no effect on Sepolia and no value at risk. A mirror-unique chain id would bind the txs to this chain only.

**h-web**

- fisco-model.ts:183 / fisco-cards.tsx:50-54: under a green verdict, the F1 and M1 stop cards show 'says' (the Error(string) in native.output) as the chain's own words. No verifier check binds that field: view.ts checkNative checks only the hash, block and status of refused steps, and regulator.ts checks outputs only for G/V steps. So any printable ASCII up to 120 chars in an unanchored (or operator-built) pack is shown next to 'Refused by the chain' under 'N of N checks passed'. Show it only when it equals the known FISCO texts for status 22 and 18, and otherwise fall back to the catalogue's expectedError.
- fisco-cards.tsx:125-136: the validator and observer chips come from chain.json sealerCount and observerCount, which are only schema-bounded (1..16, 0..16) and not cross-checked. They are shown as fact under a green verdict.
- fisco-cards.tsx:170-181 / fisco-model.ts:303-305: the Timestamp card prints the sidecar's block number and UTC time as the public timestamp ('Anyone can check that this pack existed by then'). checkSepoliaAnchor checks block and receipt only against each other, so consistent edits of receipt.blockNumber, receipt.blockHash, block.number, block.hash and block.timestamp still pass offline (the live test anchor-sh.live.test.ts:99-101 shows served receipt fields are not bound offline). An operator could backdate the displayed time. The CLI's caveat ('inclusion is confirmed online (--anchor-rpc) or on Etherscan') is dropped. Label the block and time as stated by the sidecar, to be confirmed on Etherscan.
- fisco-section.tsx:89: TimestampCard is not given 'proven', so an anchor that passes while another check fails still shows 'Public timestamp' with an Etherscan link under the red verdict. e2e/smoke/evidence-fisco.spec.ts expectNotVerified asserts no Etherscan link under a red verdict, but only its tamper fixtures, where the anchor also fails, exercise that.
- fisco-model.ts:57-58 safeDetail does not replace U+061C, U+200B-U+200D, U+2060-U+2064 or U+FEFF (invisible or bidi marks). It is only used on failure details under a red verdict.
- fisco-section.tsx:58: the green header's 'replayed <date>' uses the API listing's createdAt, not the browser-verified pack.json. Separately, the single pack checked is the newest by pack.json createdAt (fisco-store.ts:169), so a later-dated failing pack hides a verified one (display only, never a pass).
- packages/api/src/evidence/store.ts:47 readInside uses fh.readFile() and does not cap the read at the fstat size. The mock's FISCO path now uses this reader instead of the mock's own capped readUpTo, so a file growing between fstat and read (local writer only) is read whole.
- packages/api-mock/src/fisco.ts: every getFiscoFile request re-runs the synchronous source-bundle tenancy parse (up to 3 x 4 MiB) and the pack walk, up to 400 times per Proof page view. Memoize per pack or per short window.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (unchanged in the range): actions are pinned by mutable major tags (checkout@v7, dorny/paths-filter@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v6, setup-node@v7, foundry-rs/foundry-toolchain@v1), and gitleaks 8.30.1 is downloaded with curl with no checksum. The jobs are read-only-permission and secret-free pull_request jobs, so this is pinning hygiene, not a privilege path.
- .github/CODEOWNERS: the browser code that decides the FISCO pass (apps/web/components/evidence/served-fisco.ts, fisco-anchor-check.ts, fisco-model.ts) and the mock's FISCO tenancy (packages/api-mock/src/fisco.ts) are owned by the P2 lines, not by P1, who owns tools/verify-evidence. Consider adding explicit P1 lines if code-owner review is enforced.
